selections.description: Keep the TypeScript parser behavior aligned with the Rust reference, not its implementation language.
acceptance: Shared fixtures produce equivalent parsed values and error classifications.
Relevant upstream regression cases have corresponding target tests for Unicode, offsets, and boundary behavior.
The configured target typecheck and parser parity tests pass without changing their assertions.

instructions.goal: Port the selected Rust parser behavior into the existing TypeScript parser so the target has the same observable values and error categories while retaining its own public API.
adaptation: Use the target's existing TypeScript types, module layout, and error conventions; translate behavior rather than Rust syntax.
Use shared fixtures and add focused target regression tests for each relevant upstream behavior change.
Keep byte-offset behavior explicit where JavaScript string indices differ from Rust byte offsets; block if the existing API cannot express the required result safely.
nonGoals: Do not add a Rust runtime, FFI, parser generator, or new dependency.
Do not change target-only helpers in src/shared/target-parser-helpers.ts or silently change the exported TypeScript API.
Do not broaden the selection to unrelated parser features or rewrite protected test fixtures.

preserve: Keep src/shared/target-parser-helpers.ts and the target's public TypeScript exports unchanged.
Preserve the target's error-handling conventions; report blocked if parity requires an unapproved API change.
